free_tier.stated: N/A. Front-end to rclone storage backends, inheriting free tiers of supported providers. Documentation lists Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Mega, pCloud, Box, Yandex, Jottacloud, WebDAV, FTP, SFTP, Swift, B2, and S3.

per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Determined by the selected rclone backend. Rclone handles throttling and retries across remote endpoints.

tooling: Two paths: (a) `git annex initremote type=rclone ..`. Native, no extra install, documented via `rclone gitannex -h`; (b) the older `git-annex-remote-rclone` bash script (DanielDent, ~300 lines). rclone itself is a single static binary.
chaining: Combines git-annex versioning, checksum verification, and partial checkouts with rclone remote storage backends. A single repository can configure multiple rclone remotes across diverse storage providers using git annex copy commands.
limits_note: Per-backend: file size caps, per-day upload quotas, API rate limits all apply unchanged. rclone's Drive backend has its own 750 GB/day upload cap; OneDrive throttles. Encrypted annex remotes lose rclone's server-side dedupe.

extras.quota_verbatim: N/A — front-end to rclone's ~70 backends, so it inherits every free tier already catalogued by the other C-slots. The docs' own list (still current) names Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Mega, pCloud, Box, Yandex, Jottacloud, WebDAV, FTP, SFTP, Swift, B2, S3.
extras.limits_verbatim: Per-backend: file size caps, per-day upload quotas, API rate limits all apply unchanged. rclone's Drive backend has its own 750 GB/day upload cap; OneDrive throttles. Encrypted annex remotes lose rclone's server-side dedupe.
extras.egress_verbatim: Inherited from the rclone backend; rclone throttles/retries but does not pay for egress.
extras.chaining_verbatim: The strongest multiplier in this slot: annex gives you versioning + hash verification + partial clone, rclone gives you ~70 free-tier backends. One annex repo can have a dozen rclone remotes across a dozen free accounts of different providers, with `git annex copy --to` fanning out. This is literally the 'google-drive-service-account' pattern applied to large-file versioning.
extras.tooling_verbatim: Two paths: (a) `git annex initremote type=rclone ...` — native, no extra install, documented via `rclone gitannex -h`; (b) the older `git-annex-remote-rclone` bash script (DanielDent, ~300 lines). rclone itself is a single static binary.
